Boy killed after allegedly being hit by JCB during SP rally in Gorakhpur; BJP slams SP ‘hooliganism’; Akhilesh demands high-level probe
 Five local SP leaders and 66 unidentified party workers were booked in connection with the death of the 14-year-old boy, the son of a BJP worker, who was allegedly hit by a JCB during PDA Rath Yatra in Gorakhpur on November 18
 Updated - November 19, 2026 10:45 pm IST - Lucknow 
 Mayank Kumar READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav demanded a high-level investigation into the incident.. File
 | Photo Credit: PTI
 A war of words erupted on Thursday (November 19, 2026) over the death of a 14-year-old boy, who was allegedly killed after being hit by a bulldozer during a Samajwadi Party (SP) roadshow led by party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Gorakhpur. While the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) blamed SP hooliganism, Mr. Yadav demanded a high-level investigation into the incident.
 “This video is evidence that the U.P. CM is blaming others without any proof regarding the unfortunate death of a youth in Gorakhpur, which is highly condemnable and an example of very low-level politics. The video clearly shows that there was neither a roadshow nor a rally, despite what the Chief Minister claims. By politicising this accident, the bereaved family is also being treated unfairly. There should be a high-level investigation into this accident so that the truth is revealed,” Mr. Yadav posted on X, alongside a video showing normal traffic movement.
 Turn your bulldozer towards EC: Akhilesh Yadav taunts CM Yogi Adityanath The SP president added, “Heartless and insensitive people only engage in politics; only family members can truly understand the pain of losing a child. We are all deeply saddened by the death of an innocent child and express our deepest condolences to the family. We have asked our team to meet them and provide all possible support. Those politicising this unfortunate incident should remember how they mistreated and threatened the grieving mother of the young victim in the Lucknow fire. The public sees through the pretense of those who pretend to mourn.”
 Five local SP leaders and 66 unidentified party workers were booked in connection with the death of the 14-year-old boy, the son of a BJP worker, who was allegedly hit by a JCB during Mr. Yadav’s PDA Rath Yatra in Gorakhpur on November 18.
 In the First Information Report (FIR), the father of the deceased alleged that a speeding JCB, which was part of the SP chief’s roadshow, hit his son, Aryavardhan Singh, and that the driver and rally organisers fled the scene. The police registered a case under Sections 281 (negligent driving) and 106(1) (causing death by a rash or negligent act) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
 Akhilesh pitches Gorakhpur vs Kashi narrative, eyes inroads among Brahmins, business community U.P. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party, describing the incident as a brutal murder. “A teenager who came from Jhangaha to Gorakhpur for his studies fell victim to the SP roadshow. Those who patronise the mafia remained silent and did not offer even a word of condolence,” Mr. Adityanath said in Gorakhpur.
 Mr. Adityanath said he has issued strict instructions to the administration to identify the goons responsible for creating chaos on the roads and ensure they receive stringent punishment.
 “‘ Kutte ki poonch kabhi seedhi nahi ho sakt i (A dog’s tail can never be straightened). These goons and mafias can only be brought into line through the full force of the law. Roads in the State were built to ensure smooth movement for the general public, not to facilitate the lawlessness of SP and Congress goons. If anyone dares to revive mafia-style activities, it will not take long to crush them completely,” he said.
 Dalits in Gorakhpur face more injustice than anywhere else, alleges Akhilesh After meeting the victim’s family, Mr. Adityanath said, “The 14-year-old was returning from school. After being hit by a JCB, he was deliberately run over by a vehicle and killed. The actions of the Samajwadi Party chief and the conduct of his goons are bringing shame upon shame. Aren’t these people ashamed of themselves?... This hooliganism will not be tolerated in Uttar Pradesh… I have personally come here to express my condolences. Action will be taken against every goon who has created disorder here and attempted to create an atmosphere of fear and terror.”
 In a cautious note, Mr. Yadav asked SP leaders not to use bulldozers for rallies. “A bulldozer’s work is to build quality roads. The truth is that a bulldozer has no brain of its own; it has a driver,” said Mr. Yadav.
